full_name: Royal Ashdown Forest Golf Club (Old Course)

summary.text: The Old Course at Royal Ashdown Forest is a heathland course in East Sussex with no sand bunkers, laid out in the Ashdown Forest.

setting.text: Top100golfcourses says it affords long views from the high parts across the forest and the rolling Sussex countryside.
The challenge comes from undulating land, streams, heather, bracken and many trees.
The only bunkers are natural grassy pits.
Ashdown Forest is protected by Acts of Parliament, so no alterations to the terrain are allowed without the conservators' approval.

history.text: The club was founded in 1888 as the Ashdown Forest & Tunbridge Wells Golf Club, by brothers William and Francis Lee, Robert Birch and the Reverend A. T. Scott. The course opened the following year.
Queen Victoria gave royal patronage in 1893, and Tunbridge Wells was dropped from the name in 1901.
It was originally only about 4,900 yards and was gradually lengthened between 1910 and 1920 to over 6,400.
Bernard Darwin wrote that at the end of a round we realise 'with pleasurable shock that there is not a single hideous rampart or so much as a pot bunker'.
New drainage went into fourteen greens in 2016, alongside a ten-year tree clearing programme.
There have been only five head professionals in the club's history, according to Top100golfcourses.

trivia.text: Winnie the Pooh's creator A. A. Milne and his son Christopher Robin were both members, Christopher playing mainly on the West Course.
Abe Mitchell, who lost the 1920 Open to George Duncan, was a member of the club's artisan section, the Cantelupe Club.
Top100golfcourses lists the course as par 72, though it measures just over 6,400 yards.

6.text: The par 3 6th is the 'Island Hole', only 125 yards from the medal tees but ringed by a deep stream and a gully, with a ridge across the green.

17.text: The 17th is a downhill par 4 of 480 yards from the back tees, needing a second shot across gorse, bracken and a path.

local.text: The forest is the setting for Winnie the Pooh. Top100golfcourses says Pooh invented Poohsticks on the edge of the woods.
The club's postcode is RH18, in East Sussex.
